headline: High: nullclaw can read/write shared workspaces and use broad network/MCP, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways with great_expectations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: great_expectations reads and writes files under data sources, validation results, and documentation, while nullclaw can read_filesystem, write_filesystem, use_mcp, and process stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible default path where nullclaw ingests great_expectations outputs as trusted content. No direct provenance controls are shown, so injection risk is real but not clearly high.
conditions: IF nullclaw reads great_expectations validation results or documentation as instructions
IF both agents share ~/.nullclaw/workspace or another common directory
IF MCP or stdin/stdout is used to pass untrusted file content between them
mitigations: Separate workspaces so great_expectations outputs are not auto-read by nullclaw
Disable MCP routes for file-backed prompts
Require a human review step before nullclaw acts on validation reports
Prefix all great_expectations outputs with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: great_expectations touches validation results and documentation, and nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, conversation history, and secrets such as API keys and private keys. Because nullclaw has broad network egress and filesystem access, a shared workspace could expose sensitive artifacts from either side. The pair is not proven to share a workspace by default, so medium is the right floor.
conditions: IF great_expectations writes validation results into a directory nullclaw can read
IF nullclaw is configured to ingest workspace files into its context
IF either agent stores secrets or sensitive data in the shared directory
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared workspace
Restrict nullclaw read access to a dedicated subdirectory
Rotate or redact sensitive files before handoff
Turn off automatic file ingestion in nullclaw
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: great_expectations writes data sources, validation results, and documentation, while nullclaw can write_filesystem and modify_git_state. If they operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The rubric’s high indicator fits because both have write capability and no locking or coordination primitive is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF nullclaw commits or rewrites files that great_expectations also updates
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add a manual lock file before writes
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations produces validation results that nullclaw can read_filesystem and then act on through shell, browser, git, or MCP tools. That makes A’s output a likely input to B’s decisions, and the profile does not show a verification gate. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, but not enough evidence shows automatic harmful action, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF nullclaw treats validation results as authoritative without cross-checking
IF great_expectations outputs are fed directly into nullclaw task prompts
IF nullclaw is allowed to execute shell or git actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Require a second-pass human review of validation summaries
Compare validation results against raw source data before acting
Disable auto-execution from report text
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for report ingestion
requires-engineering: add structured schemas and verification checks

E_compliance.rationale: great_expectations is a data-engineering tool with files for data sources and validation results, while nullclaw handles audit logs, workspace files, and secrets. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported: shared handling of regulated data could create policy gaps if the same workspace is reused. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise workspace handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents
IF audit logs capture sensitive validation artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Set short retention on audit logs
Redact secrets before validation runs
Document which agent owns deletion requests
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
